subject: How to use space-time LGCP model to predict the next time point

messages.author: 616d580ea96dab5b
messages.subject: How to use space-time LGCP model to predict the next time point
parts:
Hi INLA users,

I am fitting a space-time log Gaussian Cox process model with covariates. I want to fit 7 days of data to predict the spatial distribution on the 8th day.

I refer to SPDE BOOK section 8.3, and fitting 7 days of data, at this time tmesh length is 7, but I don't know how to deal with the 8th day of data.

My code is similar to the SPDE BOOK 8.3 section example, so assuming that in the SPDE BOOK 8.3 section example, I want to fit the data from the first 5 time nodes to predict the data for the 6th time node, what should I do.

Any help is greatly appreciated.

messages.author: 616d580ea96dab5b
messages.subject: Re: How to use space-time LGCP model to predict the next time point
parts:
PS, I have 14 days of point pattern data. I want use 7 days of data to fit an LGCP model, then use this to predict the next days(the 8th day). Performing this over a 14 day period means that we first use the first 7 days to predict the eighth day, then use days 2 – 8 (the actual day 8th data, not the predictions) to predict day 9 and so on.

Hi INLA users,

After I fitted the Spatial-Temporal LGCP model with INLA, I checked the model fit with CPO and PIT.

I found that sum (model $ cpo $ failure) is zero. If I understand correctly, this should be a better result. 

However, when the distribution of PIT is checked, as shown in the figure below, the results do not seem to be uniformly distributed. 

Considering that the response variable Y in STLGCP is only 0 and 1, does this indicate that even the PIT is not uniformly distributed, but the prediction is still consistent with the data.

Thanks any help!

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: How to use space-time LGCP model to predict the next time point
parts:
PIT is originally defined for continous response. It is less clear how
to do this properly for discrete responses, in particular binary data!

Best
H
